title: Where does the folded paper strip end?
description: A paper strip is folded in half and its end falls between two tenth marks. Each tenth is split into ten parts, the small part gets its name, and the length is written in two ways. Keeko doubts the size of the small part.
teaching_notes: One idea: splitting each tenth into ten parts makes a unit of one hundred parts, and one part is a hundredth. Watch for students who call the new small part a tenth because it sits inside a tenth.

source: A paper strip 8 9/10 units long is folded in half. Its new length ends between 4 4/10 and 4 5/10. Split each tenth into 10 parts: what is one small part, and where does the folded strip end? Can the length also be said as 4 units and 45 hundredths?
video_script.why: The child can name tenths but meets a length that falls between two tenth marks, so a smaller part is needed.
video_script.substitution: Split each tenth into ten parts, so a unit has one hundred parts and one part is a hundredth.
video_script.anchor: A paper strip folded in half, with its end between the 4 4/10 mark and the 4 5/10 mark of a unit scale
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko calls the small part one tenth because it lies inside a tenth, but a tenth is cut into 10 parts, so one part is only 1/100 of a unit.
video_script.payoff_line: The folded strip is four units and forty five hundredths long

final_answer.spoken: four units, four tenths and five hundredths, which is also four units and forty five hundredths

maths_rules: Each tenth is split into 10 parts; a unit has 10 tenths, so 10 × 10 = 100 parts.
One part is 1/100 of a unit, a hundredth.
The strip ends 5 parts after the 4 4/10 mark, so it is 4 units, 4 tenths and 5 hundredths.
10 hundredths make 1 tenth, so 4 tenths = 40 hundredths and 40 + 5 = 45 hundredths.
Slip: the small part is not 1/10, it is 1/100.
video_script.design: One idea: a unit split into tenths and each tenth into ten parts has one hundred parts, and one part is a hundredth. Assumes the child knows tenths. Wrong idea: the small part is a tenth. The strip and its scale stay all video; the zoomed gap builds in the ground part.
